english.quote:
Proof of English Proficiency
All applicants of the M.Sc. Computer Science program are required to upload valid* proof of
a working knowledge of the English language of at least level C1 before the application
deadline.
Accepted proofs are:
• TOEFL IBT 95 points / from 2026: 5 or better
• IELTS band 7.0 or better (academic)
• Cambridge ESOL CAE/CPE University of Cambridge ESOL exams
• Oxford Test of English Advanced (C1)
• PTE Academic Score 76 or better
• telc: telc University B2/C1 (result „very good“); telc C1 / C2 (general examination)
*Please note that most certificates, e.g. TOEFL-certificate, IELTS-certificate etc., are only
valid for two years. The uploaded certificate has to be valid at least until the application
deadline (15th of January/July).
“Medium of Instruction (MOI)”, e.g. certificate confirming your bachelor’s program was
conducted in English, is not accepted.
If you are a national with citizenship and education in one of the countries listed below, you
do not need to upload one of the English proficiency proofs listed above. In this case, it is
mandatory to upload a proof of citizenship instead (readable copy of a passport or similar).
In case of questions, please contact the Student Advisor, Dr. Stefanie Anstein.
List of majority native English speaking countries currently used by the Admission
Committee:
• Antigua and Barbuda
• Australia
• The Bahamas
• Barbados
• Belize
• Canada (except Quebec)
• Dominica
• Grenada
• Guyana
• Ireland
• Jamaica
• Malta
• New Zealand
• St Kitts and Nevis
• St Lucia
• St Vincent and the Grenadines
• Trinidad and Tobago
• United Kingdom
• United States of America
As of January, 2026

deadlines.quote: Application period for the winter semester: November 15 – January 15 The winter semester starts in October. summer semester: May 15 – July 15 The summer semester starts in April.

selection_process.value: On the basis of the documents presented, the Board of Admission (Zulassungsausschuss) decides whether the conditions of entry are fulfilled or not. In case of the latter, an interview or an entrance examination may be necessary. In some cases, students who are missing certain qualifications may be granted admission on the condition that they acquire these qualifications in the course of their studies, for example by attending additional modules.
